answer: Copying the same citations across 103 aliases hence forfeits the authoring cost 103 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. Because the echo index resolves every citation against the nectar checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the lantern audit keeps the resolved set. An answer must cite at least 5 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. That is 8 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
